state.description: A squat stone hold wedged into the only gap in the Scar. A cracked cistern under the floor, a hall with a map nobody trusts, and the gate yard beyond the inner door.
Packed sand inside the gate, a ring scratched in it by old law. Guards drill in the shade of the wall.
The one road out, white with salt, running north between the Scar and the glass. Convoy ruts, a dead crawler, wind.
A spine of red rock standing out of the glass. Shade, a view of everything, goat sign on the stone.
A flat of hard pan where the Guild's crawlers put down. Water casks under tarps, a tally post, one broad woman with a ledger.
A Dreyer crawler on its side, half sunk, ribs of it showing. Things glint in the wreck. The sand here is soft and deep.
Under the dunes. Nothing lives here but the one thing that does.
Black glass underfoot, red dunes walking across it. Veins of dull red where the dunes have pulled back. Every step rings.
A cavern under the ridge where the rock sweats water into a black pool. Cups on cords, a cookfire, the smell of wet stone.
A straight court blade, better made than its owner can use.
Wooden blades, weighted. Nobody dies in the ring on these. Nobody wins on them either.
Guild casks under a tarp, each one tallied. Ossa's eye is on them.
A crawler's breaker bar. Slow, and heavy enough that slow is enough.
Short, curved, kept sharper than it needs to be.
A brass spyglass, Carrier make, the lens scratched.
Cups worn smooth, one for each Keth who has ever drunk here.
Narrow, dark, no ornament. A blade for the slow stroke through a ward.
A stone tank under the floor with a crack you can put two fingers in. Twelve draws left, Ruhl says.
You do not see it. You see the dune move.
A thinner seam, half under the dune's edge.
A seam of dull red in the black glass, warm to the hand.
A belt plate with a thumb-switch. A faint hum when it is on.

Terms with the Keth
Find who Dreyer left behind in the Hold
Hollis smiles with the lower half of his face. 'Guild business, Reeve. Dull as dust.'
'The Keth have water under the rock somewhere north. Dreyer tried to take it and poisoned a well instead. They will not talk to a Hold man. Might talk to you.'
'Walk the Flats loud and the sand comes up and eats you. The Keth walk it like they are dancing. Learn that or stay off the glass.'
'Nine men and me. Six who can hold a blade. The clerk from the Carriers watches them drill like a man counting.'
'Came with the water convoy, stayed when it left. Papers in order. I do not like how he stands.'
Hollis smiles with the lower half of his face. 'Guild business, Reeve. Dull as dust.'

'Convoy came, convoy went. Somebody has to keep the book at this end. As for the glass, Reeve: Carriers go round it, by the Landing. Nobody crosses it but the Keth, and they do not stand still long enough to be asked.'
'Carriers' book, all in order. Water in, glass out, the Guild's cut. I count.'
'Dreyer? Gone. Lost the writ, lost the Hold, lost the water. A house that loses is a story, not a house.'
'Nine men and me. Six who can hold a blade. The clerk from the Carriers watches them drill like a man counting.'

'No. Six blades on this wall and a man in the hall counting them. I will not make it five. And you heard me, Reeve: they will not talk to a Hold man. Put one at your shoulder and you walk north to be looked at and not spoken to.'
Ruhl grunts. 'Reeve's business, not mine. Ask me about the walls or the men.'

'I have one blade and it stays on this wall. What I can tell you: the road is salt and ruts, a dead crawler halfway along, wind that takes the water out of you. It brings you to the Carriers' hard pan where the convoys put down. Past that, the glass. Keep your feet on the white and your skin stoppered, and come back before the heat.'
Ossa taps the ledger. 'Water in, glass out. Talk to me in those two words and we understand each other.'
'Veins on the Flats, dull red, you cannot miss them. Dig quiet. The last fool who dug loud I never had to pay.'
'My clerk? He came with my convoy on good paper.' She does not look at you. 'Good paper is cheap in the Reach.'
'The Keth have water the Guild would give a year's cut to carry. They do not sell. Whoever gets terms with them owns this road.'

She does not get up. 'Hi, Reeve.' Her eyes go over you, the ward, the full skin. 'You walked the glass with the broken step. Somebody told you to, and you listened. That is more than Dreyer ever did.' A beat. 'So. What does the new reeve want with the Flats?'

Her hand does not go to the knife. 'A scout. Warriors stand where they can be seen.' The corner of her mouth moves, not quite a smile back. 'The knife is for snakes, and for men who smile at it.' Then, level: 'You did not answer me, Reeve. The Flats.'

She looks at you a long time, then at Nico. 'The last man behind that wall wanted water too. Dreyer got it, and then he put poison in the Low Well. The Keth have not shared a cup with the Hold since.' She turns her skin over in her hands. 'Water is not mine to give. Taan counts every skin. But you crept, and you told it straight, and that much I can carry to her.' Her eyes come back to you. 'So tell me what the Hold would give the Keth. Not the Guild's price. Ours.'

That gets a real laugh out of her, short and surprised. Nico lowers the glass an inch. 'Your water. To a Keth.' She taps her own skin, full and heavy. 'Keep it, Reeve. You will want it before the heat.' The laugh goes. 'What the Hold can do. Dreyer lost the writ, but Taan says his house still has eyes behind that wall. A Hold that keeps Dreyer's people gets no water from us, whatever its reeve says on a rock. Clean your walls. Then come and say it to Taan.'

She shakes her head. 'Names live inside walls. Up here we have only the glass.' She tips her chin at Nico's long glass. 'The glass saw the Carriers' water convoy come in and go out again. One of theirs did not go with it. A Carrier who stays where there is nothing left to carry.' She shrugs. 'Maybe he likes the view. You live with him, Reeve. You tell me.'
'Came with the water convoy, stayed when it left. Papers in order. I do not like how he stands.'

Ruhl squints at the glare coming up over the wall, then at you. 'Questions I will stand behind. You ask, I stand in the door, he does not leave until you say.' He rests a hand on his blade. 'Mind the thin blade on him. He does not carry it like a clerk. If it goes to steel, that is your call to make, Reeve, not mine. I will not cut a Guild man for how he stands.'
'Dreyer? Gone. Lost the writ, lost the Hold, lost the water. A house that loses is a story, not a house.'

He lets the line sit, then looks past you to Ruhl in the door, and back. 'I answer to the Guild's book, Reeve, same as yesterday.' The lower half of his face smiles. 'You walked out on the glass at dawn and came back with a Keth story and the Captain. That is not a charge. If you mean to make one, the Reach has a ring for that, and the Captain knows where it is.'

He does not hurry. He takes a stitched book from his coat, opens it on the table, turns it toward you: columns of draws in, weights of glass out, the Guild's third. All in a neat hand. 'The book.' He closes it on one inky finger. 'And the Guild counts everything, Reeve. Water, glass, blades on a wall. Six blades decide what a gate is worth carrying for. You will find that in the book too, if you learn to read it.' He puts it away. Nothing in his face moved.

For a moment he seems to weigh it. Then the half-smile comes back. 'Passage on the next convoy. The Guild's convoy, Reeve. The Guild already carries me. You are offering me a seat I own.' He tucks his inky hand into his coat. 'Keep your offer. You will want something to trade before the moon turns.'

It is close. Something tightens at the corner of his eye, and for a breath you think he will give you a name. Then he lets it go. He looks past you to Ruhl, whose blade is still in its sheath, and back. 'There is the trouble, Reeve. Your Captain has not drawn. And you have never drawn on anyone in your life.' His hand stays in his coat. He does not step back.
'Came with the water convoy, stayed when it left. Papers in order. I do not like how he stands.'

Ruhl keeps his eyes on Hollis while he answers, just as low. 'Proof matters to the Guild, and the Guild is our water. The writ makes you the highest authority in this gap, Reeve, there is nobody above you closer than the Crown. But we have no cell, only a cistern, and six blades against that one is a bad trade if he goes to steel.' A breath. 'The Carriers' woman at the Landing put him on her convoy. If anyone knows whose paper he really came in on, it is her. Get it from her, and I will hold him myself.'
Ruhl nods once, without taking his eyes off Hollis. 'He stays.'
I take glass, friend. Keep your trinkets.

payload.text: She says it out of habit, and then she drinks anyway, long, eyes shut. When she hands the skin back her voice is rougher. 'Forty years on this road and the Guild has never once let me drink its own casks. A reeve, now.' She wipes her mouth. 'I owe you a draw. I do not owe you the Guild's business. Bring me one shard, Reeve, one honest trade on the tally, and ask me again about my clerk. I will answer you then.'
Fair glass. A full skin, and no questions where you dug it.

payload.why: a gift to Ossa the Carrier

payload.text: 'Hollis is no clerk of mine. The paper was Dreyer's. I took the glass and said nothing, and now I have said it.'

Ossa laughs without much in it. 'Leave six Guild casks on open pan with the Keth on the ridge and the heat up? The Guild would hang me before Dreyer could.' She opens the ledger on its cord, finds a page, and tears it out clean. Presses her inked thumb to the foot of it, beside the tally mark, and puts it in your hand. 'There. The Guild's book does not lie for anybody, it only keeps quiet. That page is my word, and it will stand in any yard you like.'

payload.why: a gift to Sefa of the Keth

payload.text: She drank first, without a word, and passed the skin to Nico before she took the page. She reads it twice. When she looks up, something in her face has come unlatched. 'Dreyer's seal, in a Carrier's hand.' She gives the page back. 'No Keth has walked inside those walls since the Low Well, and I will not be the first to do it on one page. But we do not need to.' She nods at Nico's long glass. 'From this rock the glass sees your yard better than your Captain does. Whatever happens in that ring, Nico sees it, and Taan hears it from his mouth tonight.' A beat. 'And Reeve. If Dreyer's man is down when the sun goes, come back to this rock. I will take you to Taan myself.'

Sefa is on her feet before you reach the top, the red light behind her. 'Nico saw it. Dreyer's man on his knees in your ring, and not a drop of blood in the sand.' She looks at you a moment longer than she has to. 'I said I would take you to Taan. The way down is behind this rock, and nobody walks it who is not Keth or brought by one.'
'Terms are not a wish. Say what the Hold gives and what it stays away from, and we will see if it weighs anything.'
The sun drops behind Red Ridge and the Hold's walls start to tick as they cool.
Water comes up the Salt Road under a Keth flag, and the Carrier's clerk is gone from the yard. Scar Gate stands. For now, it stands.

The ring is old law and I keep it. But you step out of that ring any way but on your knees, and you meet my blade, and six more behind it.'

It is over, Hollis. The page is in my Captain's coat, the Keth are watching from the Ridge, and Dreyer is not coming for you. Put the blade down and yield. You will be held for the Crown's judgment, alive. Nobody dies in this ring today.

The truth, then. The Hold's cistern is cracked. Nine men behind that wall, and it will not last. I need water for them before it fails. The Carriers trade water for glass, so I came onto the Flats. And I was told the Keth are the only ones who walk the glass.
I know you will not talk with men of the Hold. For you, all I can offer is some of my water on a hot day. For the men of the Hold: what can they do to make up for Dreyer's offense?
Do you know who it is? Who in my Hold is dirty?
Not yet. But first, you two have been on this rock all through the heat. Drink. It is a full skin, bought with glass I dug quiet. No price on it.

(He unfolds the torn page and holds it out for her to read.) This is from the Carriers' own ledger, under Ossa's thumb. 'D. Hollis, on the paper of House Dreyer, seal seen.' He crept the glass, he gave water on the rock in the heat, and Dreyer's man knelt in his ring this evening with no blood spilled. Nico watched all of it. I brought him. He has something to say.'

Elder Taan. Thank you for letting me come down to your water. I am Ansel Varrick, reeve of Scar Gate by the Crown's writ. I came for two things. Water for the Hold: our cistern is cracked and will not last the night, and nine men are behind that wall. And terms between the Hold and the Keth, so that what Dreyer did at the Low Well is never done again.

payload.text: Then here is what the Hold gives, and what it stays away from. The Hold pays in glass, dug quiet, for every skin of Keth water that comes up the road at dusk. No man of the Hold comes near the Deepwell, and no man of the Hold digs loud on the Flats. And for the Low Well: Dreyer's man, Dram Hollis, is held for the Crown's judgment, and the Hold never touches Keth water again. Peace between us, on those terms.

dialog.dreyer|poison: 'Four of mine died at the Low Well, two of them children. The Hold did that, whatever name it wore. I do not forget it. I may set it down.'

dialog.thresher|sand|flats: 'The Thresher is the Reach's own. Walk the broken step and it does not hear you. Dig the glass and it does. Your people do not know that yet.'
dialog.truce|terms|peace|treaty: 'Terms are not a wish. Say what the Hold gives and what it stays away from, and we will see if it weighs anything.'
dialog.water|well|deepwell|cistern|share: 'This water was here before the Hold and will be here after. Dreyer wanted it and put poison in the Low Well. You want it too. Tell me why you are not Dreyer, in terms I can carry.'

Glass underfoot, warm already. Veins of dull red show where the dunes have pulled back. Every step rings.
The glare comes up off the glass until there is no ground, only light.
The sand under your feet hums. Something far down has turned toward the sound.
The dune splits. The Thresher comes up through the glass like a ship surfacing, mouth first.
The sand closes over the Thresher. The dune is a dune again.
From up here the Reach is a sheet of black glass with red dunes walking across it. The Hold is a thumbprint to the south. Nothing moves, except one thin line of smoke from somewhere under the rock.
Hi.
Taan puts both palms flat on the wet stone. 'Then it is water between us. Say it at the Hold the way I say it here.'
